prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics of materials and solids, and kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of knowledge on the main criteria for the selection, verification and sizing of constructive solutions for mechanical systems and components. These knowledge, integrating notions acquired in subjects of science of constructions, applied mechanics and mechanical technology, deepen design methodologies, so that students acquire awareness of the broader context of mechanical and industrial engineering, with a clear reference to aspects concerning materials, structural mechanics, mechanical systems and production technologies.

Ability to use appropriate techniques and tools to solve engineering problems, applying technical and safety standards, concerning the analysis and design of machine components or simple mechanical systems. This ability is expressed through professional skills that manifest in awareness of engineering aspects, also related to safety, such as: 1. the ability to identify suitable constructive solutions to achieve expected performance, both using consolidated architectures and introducing elements of innovation; 2. the ability to identify and apply the most suitable calculation method for the analysis and sizing of machine elements; 3. the ability to appropriately choose materials and constructive technologies for the realization of mechanical components; 4. the ability to choose standard components from catalogs for the design of simple mechanical systems.

The solution of exercises and simple constructive problems, carried out during practice sessions, contributes to improving both the ability to select relevant information and the degree of autonomy of judgment.
In the discussion of the assignments, students exercise the ability to communicate information, ideas and solutions with adequate technical language proficiency.

syllabus_topics: Mechanics of materials from the mechanical designer's perspective
Review of important machine components, with illustration of main design and verification relationships and procedures
Notes on engineering materials and main quantities of interest for the mechanical designer
Concept of damage to a mechanical component and safety factor
Design and verification procedures for components subjected to high-cycle fatigue
Damage accumulation models in variable load conditions
Mounting systems: keys, splines, splined profiles
Gear transmissions: cylindrical gears with straight and helical teeth, bevel gears
Radial, axial and angular contact rolling bearings
Fixed fasteners: notes on the calculation of welds according to UNI-EN 10011
assessment_rules: The assessment takes place through a written and an oral exam, to be taken in the same session. To access the oral exam, students must first achieve a passing grade (at least 18 out of 30 points) in the written exam. For the overall evaluation to be positive, a passing grade (at least 18 out of 30 points) must also be achieved in the oral exam. The overall grade is given by the average of the grades obtained in the two exams. In-course tests will be considered as integral to the oral exam.
